formulaText.firstTimeInstall: An installation scores 1 when no corrective-maintenance case names the same serial within {days} days after the installation's TimeLine end date; 0 when one does.
formulaText.firstTimeFix: A CM case scores 1 when no later CM names the same serial within {days} days of it being reported; 0 when one does.
formulaText.sla: The case was checked within the board's configured SLA days of being reported: RE Action date minus Open Date. Exactly the limit counts as within. No action date recorded means unknown, not a breach. Neither board has a close date, so this is time-to-first-action, not time-to-close.
formulaText.totalCmCases: Installations are counted in the month their TimeLine ends; CM cases in the month they were reported. Each board may name a category column (Job Type, Type of case) and the values that count as a KPI case; rows outside that list are synced and archived but not counted here.
formulaText.repeatedWork: A CM case counts as repeated when a later CM names the same serial within {days} days of it being reported. The exact complement of First Time Fix, over the same cases: the two always add to 100%.

apiNotes.bucketing: Installations are counted in the month their TimeLine ends; CM cases in the month they were reported.
apiNotes.matching: Both windows join on serial number alone, across boards. Tickets naming no serial cannot be matched and are counted as successes.
apiNotes.split: The installation board does not say which kind of robot a case concerns, so the serial is looked up among CM cases: the cleaning and delivery boards each handle one kind, so a serial seen on one of them identifies the robot. A case that still cannot be placed counts in the fleet total but in neither line.
apiNotes.category: Each board may name a category column and the values that count as a KPI case. Rows outside that list are synced and archived but not counted. A follow-up CM is still a follow-up whatever its category.

how.title: How the link works
how.intro: Three things connect RAASPAL to the sheet. Nothing is copied or moved — AOT keeps working in their sheet exactly as now.
how.link: The link says which sheet. The long code between /d/ and /edit is the sheet's id; it is all the system needs from the link.
how.share: The Share list says who may read it. The sheet is shared with one more “person”: RAASPAL's system account, as a Viewer. It can read; it can never edit.
how.key: A key proves the system is that account. Google gives the account a key file; the server keeps it and uses it to sign in. Without the key, the share does nothing; without the share, the key opens nothing.
how.browser: You being able to open the sheet in your browser does not help the server: it has no browser and cannot sign in as you, which is why it needs its own account.

account.title: Create the system account (once)
account.who: Whoever manages RAASPAL's Google Cloud — about 5 minutes
account.project: Open console.cloud.google.com and pick or create a project (e.g. raaspal-ops).
account.create: IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Create service account. Name it raaspal-sheets-reader. Skip the role and user steps — it needs no project permissions.
account.key: Open the new account → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. A .json file downloads.
account.email: Note the account's email on its page (…@….iam.gserviceaccount.com) — the sheet is shared with that address.
account.policy: If Google says key creation is disabled, your organisation blocks it by policy; a Google Workspace admin has to allow it for this project.

server.title: Give the key to the server
server.who: Whoever runs the backend — never paste it into chat, git or this page
server.laptop: On a laptop: keep the file outside the code folder (e.g. ~/.config/raaspal/sheets-key.json) and add one line to application-local.properties:
server.host: On the server (Lightsail): add GOOGLE_SHEETS_CREDENTIALS to api.env with the file base64-encoded (base64 -i sheets-key.json), then redeploy (deploy/deploy.sh).
server.restart: Restart the backend either way. The pill at the top of the AOT tab then stops saying “no Google key on the server”.
server.leak: The key is a password for that account. If it ever leaks, delete it under Keys in Google Cloud and make a new one — the sheet's sharing does not change.

share.title: Share the sheet with the system account
share.who: The sheet's owner, or anyone with edit rights on it
share.role: Set the role to Viewer, untick Notify people, press Share (and Share anyway if Google warns it is outside the organisation).
share.viewOnly: If you only have view rights, the Share button will not let you add people — send the owner the two-page guide Report/AOT-Google-Sheet-Access-Setup.pdf (Thai and English) with the address above.

paste.title: Paste the link here, save, test
paste.who: On the AOT tab, under Sheet link & columns
paste.copy: In the sheet, copy the address bar. Open Sheet link & columns on the AOT tab and paste it into Google Sheet link.
paste.tab: Check the Tab name matches the tab at the bottom of the sheet (usually Case). Save.
paste.test: Press Test connection. It reads the sheet and writes nothing. You should see the row count and every column name, hidden ones included.
paste.stays: The link stays saved until someone changes it or presses Remove link. To point at a different sheet, paste the new link and save — that is all. Cases copied from the old sheet stay in the database under the old sheet's id, but are no longer updated or listed here.

columns.title: Choose the id and closed columns
columns.who: Sheet link & columns — agree the answers with the sheet's owner
columns.intro: The system has to know two things the sheet does not say on its own:
columns.id: Which column names each case, forever. If there is none, ask the owner to add a Case ID column and never reuse a value. Until then, do not sort the sheet or delete rows.
columns.closed: How a closed case looks. Either a status column plus the words that mean closed (e.g. Closed, Done), or a column with the date it closed. Without this, every case since 2023 would count as still open — so the sync refuses to run.
columns.retest: Fill the fields, save, and Test connection again: the Open / Closed counts should look right.

sync.title: Turn the sync on
sync.body: Tick Keep this sheet in sync and save. From then on the sheet is copied by itself — with the monday refresh every 15 minutes, and whenever someone opens the AOT tab (at most every 5 minutes); Sync now does it immediately. Each case becomes one row in RAASPAL's case table, beside the monday tickets, and the daily copy is what lets past days be reported later — the sheet itself keeps no history.

errors.title: When something goes wrong
errors.cannotOpen: “The service account cannot open spreadsheet …” — the sheet is not shared with the address in step 3, or was un-shared. Share it again.
errors.notFound: “Spreadsheet … was not found” — the link is wrong or the sheet was deleted. Paste the link again.
errors.noTab: “… has no tab named …” — the tab was renamed. Fix the Tab field (capitals matter).
errors.noKey: “No Google service-account key configured” — step 2 is not done on this server, or it was not restarted afterwards.
errors.dupIds: “These ids are on more than one row” — two cases share an id. Fix them in the sheet; nothing is synced until they are unique.
errors.noColumn: “The AOT sheet has no column named …” — a column chosen in Sheet link & columns was renamed on the sheet. Choose it again; nothing was synced.
